## Overview

Share CPU FP8/MXFP4 MoE projection execution and automatically use MXFP4 W4A8 on CPUs with native AMX-FP8 support. Extend FP8 W8A8 MoE to quantize down-projection activations, and retain explicit MXFP4 W4A16 selection through `--moe-backend cpu_mxfp4_bf16`.

## Claims

- At measured pre-rebase head `eeb4c767b7`, GPT-OSS-20B batch output throughput improves **37.0%** versus same-head explicit W4A16, and Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 improves **4.1%** versus `ff01a6b14f`. GPT-OSS single-request latency changes by less than 1% in all three pairs.
- FP8 and MXFP4 experts share projection, routing and panel-cache code, with independent projection biases and SiLU, exact GELU and GELU-tanh support; MXFP4 also retains GPT-OSS SwiGLU.
- MXFP4 W4A8 supports tensor parallelism, retains BF16 computation for tiny experts, and falls back to W4A16 without native FP8 support.

## Validation

Current head: `74211e1111`, based on upstream `a0544b13f2`.

### Post-rebase and padding validation

At `7092057a53`, a fresh CPU build and **785 tests** passed across quantization/configuration, quantized MoE, and CPU vector/INT8 factory coverage. Serving smokes passed for GPT-OSS automatic W4A8 at TP1/TP2/TP4, explicit W4A16 at TP1, and Qwen FP8 single-request and four-request batch generation. Both default-ISA benchmark execution smokes and applicable pre-commit checks passed.

The final padding patch, committed as `74211e1111`, passed:

- Existing GPT-OSS loader and CPU quantized-MoE suites: **250 passed**.
- Temporary preservation checks for signed FP4 zeros, nonzero weights with byte-zero E8M0 scales, and all-zero channels.
- GPT-OSS-20B TP4 automatic W4A8 inspection and generation: `LLM.apply_model` verified maximum-filled padding in all 24 last-rank layers and **zero block-fallback panels**, versus 69,120 with reconstructed zero padding. Workers exited cleanly.
- Applicable pre-commit checks and `git diff --check`.

The padding patch was validated before committing; its temporary logs do not embed a source hash. Native sources and binaries still match the post-rebase build.

<details>
<summary>Test commands</summary>

```bash
# Post-rebase suites: 785 passed in total.
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_cpu_quant_fused_moe.py \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_cpu_fp8_scaled_mm.py \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp4_kernel_selection.py \
  tests/quantization/test_quantization_config_args.py \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_cpu_fp8_quant.py -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_cpu_fused_moe.py \
  -k 'vec or cpu_experts_int8' -q

# Final padding patch: 250 passed.
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_gpt_oss_weight_loading.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_cpu_quant_fused_moe.py -q

git diff --name-only -z a0544b13f2 HEAD | \
  xargs -0 .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files
git diff --check a0544b13f2 HEAD
```

</details>

Kernel suites have CPU hardware CI coverage; native FP8 cases require compatible hardware/PyTorch and ran locally. GELU coverage uses synthetic inputs; no pretrained GELU-model accuracy evaluation was run.

All candidate measurements below used **`eeb4c767b7`**, before rebasing, on a native AMX-FP8 CPU, Python 3.12.14 and PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu. Each arm's package and worker-extension identities were verified. Full accuracy and throughput comparisons were not rerun after rebasing or the padding patch.

### Serving performance at `eeb4c767b7`

TP1, 8 GiB KV cache. Three serial pairs in alternating order, seed 42, temperature 0, one warmup, prefix caching disabled, eager execution, maximum batched tokens 512 and maximum sequences 128.

| Model / workload | Baseline | Candidate | Median paired change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| GPT-OSS-20B batch, output tokens/s | 161.32 | 221.35 | **+37.0%** |
| GPT-OSS-20B single-request latency, ms | 2,237.88 | 2,217.26 | **-0.8%** |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 batch, output tokens/s | 120.37 | 125.43 | **+4.1%** |

Baseline/candidate columns are medians of three runs; changes are medians of paired ratios.

- GPT-OSS compares same-head explicit `cpu_mxfp4_bf16` with automatic W4A8. Batch gains were 37.0–38.8%; single-request latency changes were -0.9% to +0.6%.
- Qwen compares `ff01a6b14f` with `eeb4c767b7`, using matching checkouts/extensions and the same client. Both select CPU_W8A8; gains ranged from 3.9–4.7%. This measures the whole branch.
- Batch: 128 requests/concurrency, 512 input and 128 output tokens. GPT-OSS single: 32 requests, concurrency 1, 128 input and 64 output tokens. All requests completed with the exact token counts.

<details>
<summary>Serving commands</summary>

Run the same configuration for each arm. GPT-OSS baseline adds `--moe-backend cpu_mxfp4_bf16`; the candidate selects automatically. For Qwen, run once from each checkout with its corresponding CPU extension.

Checkpoint revisions: GPT-OSS `6cee5e81ee83917806bbde320786a8fb61efebee`; Qwen `d206ba732169f29bb77fbf80fc2c4b81d4d30782`.

```bash
MODEL=openai/gpt-oss-20b  # Also Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8.
export LD_PRELOAD="/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libtcmalloc_minimal.so.4:$PWD/.venv/lib/libiomp5.so"
export VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=8

# GPT-OSS adds --reasoning-parser openai_gptoss.
# Qwen adds --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}'.
.venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve "$MODEL" \
  --dtype bfloat16 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --enforce-eager \
  --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-batched-tokens 512 --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --generation-config vllm \
  --seed 42

.venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench serve \
  --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --model "$MODEL" --tokenizer "$MODEL" --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 128 --random-range-ratio 0 \
  --num-prompts 128 --max-concurrency 128 --num-warmups 1 \
  --ignore-eos --seed 42 --temperature 0 \
  --save-result --result-dir results
```

Repeat in baseline/candidate, candidate/baseline, baseline/candidate order with a fresh server for each arm. For the single-request workload, use input/output lengths 128/64, 32 prompts and concurrency 1.

</details>

### Model evaluation at `eeb4c767b7`

| Evaluation | Baseline | Candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| GPT-OSS-20B GPQA, 1,584 responses per arm | 879 correct (55.49%) | 876 correct (55.30%) |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 GSM8K, 1,319 questions per arm | 1,219 correct (92.42%) | 1,212 correct (91.89%) |

GPQA uses 198 questions × eight matched presentations, temperature 1, low reasoning effort, and a 32,768-token output limit. GPT-OSS compares same-head explicit W4A16 with automatic W4A8; Qwen compares `ff01a6b14f` with `eeb4c767b7`.

For Qwen accuracy, use the serving configuration above with prefix caching enabled, `VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=32`, and thinking disabled in both arms.

```bash
.venv/bin/python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py \
  --use-chat-completions --model Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 \
  --num-shots 5 --num-questions 1319 --max-tokens 2048 \
  --temperature 0 --seed 42 --max-concurrency 128 \
  --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}' \
  --save-results gsm8k.json
```

## Details

The existing FP8 W8A8 path quantizes incoming activations per token but computes the down projection with BF16 intermediate activations. The shared projection implementation extends FP8 execution to that second stage and reuses it for MXFP4 weights, with channel normalization and block fallback for scale ranges that cannot safely use E4M3.

MXFP4 experts with at most four routed rows retain BF16 computation and unquantized intermediate activations; larger experts use FP8 for both projections. CPU W4A8 requires BF16 inputs and does not support EP. Defaults and precision tradeoffs are documented in `docs/features/quantization/online.md`.

CPU postprocessing replaces byte-zero down-projection scales with the channel maximum only for groups containing entirely zero FP4 weights. This preserves their zero contribution while preventing padded groups from forcing block normalization.

FP8 bias conversion moves into expert construction because the factory did not invoke the former loading hook. Both projection biases are handled independently and covered through the real factory path.

Builds on merged [#49942](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49942) and [#50949](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50949). October 23 open-PR searches found no duplicate; no issue is associated with this branch. [#61346](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61346) targets BF16 fallback without AMX, a different scope.

AI assistance was used for implementation, review, validation and drafting. The submitting human must review every changed line, understand the implementation and run relevant tests before submission.

+def _quantize_mxfp4(weight: torch.Tensor) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Pack BF16 weights into MXFP4 E2M1 values and E8M0 block scales."""
+    block_size = 32
+    values = torch.tensor([0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0, 6.0], dtype=torch.float32)
+    bounds = torch.tensor([0.25, 0.75, 1.25, 1.75, 2.5, 3.5, 5.0], dtype=torch.float32)
+    grouped = weight.float().reshape(-1, block_size)
+    amax = grouped.abs().amax(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
+    exponent = torch.ceil(
+        torch.maximum(torch.log2(amax / values[-1]), torch.tensor(-127.0))
+    )
+    normalized = grouped / torch.exp2(exponent)
+    magnitude = (normalized.abs().unsqueeze(-1) > bounds).sum(dim=-1)
+    sign = ((2 - torch.sign(normalized)) // 2).to(torch.uint8)
+    codes = ((sign << 3) | magnitude.to(torch.uint8)).reshape(
+        *weight.shape[:-1], weight.shape[-1]
+    )
+    packed = codes[..., 0::2] | (codes[..., 1::2] << 4)
+    scales = (exponent.squeeze(-1) + 127).to(torch.uint8)
+    return packed.contiguous(), scales.reshape(*weight.shape[:-1], -1).contiguous()
